artworks.title: The Hestia Giustiniani
artworks.artist: Roman copy after a Greek original
artworks.description: A marble statue of the veiled goddess of the hearth, a Roman copy after an early Classical Greek original of about 470 BC in the Severe style. The heavy peplos, grave frontal stance and modestly drawn veil convey Hestia's austere domestic dignity. The statue takes its name from the Giustiniani collection in Rome, where it was long held.

artworks.title: The Hestia Tapestry
artworks.description: A wool tapestry woven in Byzantine Egypt in the sixth century AD, now in the Dumbarton Oaks collection in Washington, DC. It shows the goddess enthroned as Hestia Polyolbos, 'Hestia rich in blessings', flanked by attendants bearing medallions inscribed with the gifts she bestows. It is a rare survival of the pagan goddess's imagery from a Christianizing age.
